intro: How to ask a friend, a colleague and a stranger for help, and the many ways of saying yes.
p.echar una mano.consejo: It is colloquial: «échame una mano». Nothing is really thrown: it is just a way of asking for help.
p.alcanzar.consejo: Here it is not «llegar»: «¿me alcanzas la sal?» asks someone to pass you what you cannot reach.
p.te agradecería que.glosa: I would be grateful if you…
p.te agradecería que.consejo: After «que» comes the imperfect subjunctive: «te agradecería que vinieras». With «usted»: «le agradecería que…».
p.rogar.consejo: The o becomes «ue»: «ruego», «ruegas». You say «te ruego que» plus a subjunctive: «te ruego que esperes».
p.hace falta que.consejo: It takes the subjunctive: «hace falta que llegues pronto». With «que», the verb «hace» always stays singular.
p.me harías un favor.glosa: would you do me a favour?
p.me harías un favor.consejo: The conditional «harías» softens the request. Without it you would say «¿me haces un favor?», more direct.
p.solicitar.consejo: It belongs to letters and forms: «solicito una cita». In conversation people say «pedir».
p.colaboración.consejo: It is feminine and ends in -ción: «la colaboración». It comes from «colaborar», which is to work with others.
p.con mucho gusto.consejo: You use it to accept a request gladly. It sounds warmer than a plain «sí».
p.cómo no.consejo: It looks like a question, but it is a very polite «sí»: to «¿me ayudas?» you can answer «¡cómo no!».
p.por supuesto.consejo: It is two separate words. It works to accept a request and also to confirm an idea.
p.será un placer.consejo: It is very polite and a little formal. «Será» is the future of «ser» and has an accent on the a.
p.cuando quieras.consejo: You let the other person choose the moment. With «usted» you say «cuando quiera».
p.de paso.consejo: It adds an extra action while you do another: «voy a correos y, de paso, compro sellos».
b1.titulo: The same request at three levels
b1.texto:
A request changes depending on who you are talking to.

- **Among friends:** **Échame una mano.** **¿Me alcanzas esa caja?**
- **Polite:** **¿Me harías un favor?** **Necesitaría que me echaras una mano.**
- **Formal:** **Te agradecería que me enviaras los datos.** **Te ruego que me perdones.**

Rule of tenses: after a **conditional** (agradecería, necesitaría) comes the **imperfect subjunctive**; after a **present** (ruego, hace falta) comes the **present subjunctive**.

To say yes: **por supuesto**, **cómo no**, **con mucho gusto**, **será un placer**, **cuando quieras**.
b2.f0.texto: Germán, would you do me a favour?
b2.f2.texto: I would need you to give me a hand with the move on Saturday.
b2.f3.texto: What time do I need to get there?
b2.f4.texto: I would be grateful if you arrived at nine with your brother's van.
b2.f5.texto: It will be a pleasure, Rocío.
b2.f6.texto: While I am at it, I will bring some boxes from the garage.
b4.texto:
When you ask for something with **que**, the next verb is in the subjunctive:

- Verb in the **conditional**: **agradecería que me enviaras** los datos (imperfect).
- Verb in the **present**: **ruego que me perdones** (present).
- **Hace falta que** + present: **hace falta que llegues** pronto.

To ask without the subjunctive, a question is enough: **¿Me alcanzas la cinta?** With **solicitar** or **rogar**, the request becomes more formal.
b4.e0.texto: I beg you to forgive me.
b4.e1.texto: I request your help to solve this problem.
b4.e2.texto: I would be very grateful if you called me.
b5.f0.texto: The van arrives at nine and stops in front of the building door.
b5.f1.texto: On the landing it smells of damp cardboard and fresh paint.
b5.f2.texto: The boxes pile up against the wall like small crooked towers.
b5.f3.texto: Germán climbs the steps two at a time with a box in each arm.
b5.f4.texto: From the window, Rocío hears the echo of his steps on the empty staircase.
b5.f5.texto: At midday, the living room looks like a sea of crumpled paper.
b5.f6.texto: A ray of sun crosses the room and draws a square of golden light on the floor.
b5.f7.texto: Rocío sits on a box and drinks a glass of cold water.
b5.f8.texto: The cold water tastes of metal and summer.
b5.f9.texto: Germán wipes his forehead with his sleeve and smiles, tired.
b6.o0.refuerzo: It is a request between friends: short and direct.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «rogar que» plus the subjunctive sounds formal.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It is an energetic order, not a request.
b7.frase: Le agradecería que me ____ los datos.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: after «agradecería» comes the imperfect subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is present; after a conditional the imperfect is preferred.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is conditional; after «que» you need the subjunctive.
b8.frase: Necesitaría que me echaras una mano
b8.traduccion: I would need you to give me a hand
b9.o0.refuerzo: It is a very kind yes: it accepts the request.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Exactly: it is a refusal, not an acceptance.
b9.o2.refuerzo: It is a polite yes: it accepts the request.
b9.pregunta: Which one does NOT accept the request?
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Would you do me a favour?»
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: after the present «ruego» comes the present subjunctive.
b11.o1.refuerzo: It is imperfect: it would follow a conditional, not «ruego».
b11.o2.refuerzo: It is indicative, and «ruego que» asks for the subjunctive.
b11.pregunta: Complete the request with the right verb.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «alcanzar» here means to pass something you cannot reach.
b12.o1.refuerzo: You are not asking to buy anything: you ask for the tape to be passed.
b12.o2: Que me midan con la cinta.
b12.o2.refuerzo: There is nothing to measure: it is a request for help.
b12.pregunta: What do you ask for with «¿Me alcanzas la cinta?»
p.necesitaría.consejo: From «necesitar», in the conditional: a polite way to ask for something.
p.echaras.consejo: «echar una mano» means help someone. The subjunctive «echaras» follows «que».
p.furgoneta.consejo: Think of «furgón» plus «-eta»: a small van for carrying things.
p.garaje.consejo: The j sounds like h: «garaje» is pronounced ga-RA-he.
p.perdones.consejo: From «perdonar». Here it means forgiving someone, in the subjunctive.
p.solicito.consejo: «solicito» is formal language, typical of letters and offices.
p.resolver.consejo: The v sounds like b in Spanish: «resolver» is rre-sol-BER.
p.agradecería.consejo: «agradecería» softens a request: it is a polite conditional from «agradecer».
p.húmedo.consejo: Its root is «humedad», so think of moisture in the air.
p.apilan.consejo: Think of «pila»: things stacked one on top of another.
p.torres.consejo: Plural of «torre». The double r sounds strong: «torres».
p.torcidas.consejo: From «torcer», to twist. Crooked things are no longer straight.
p.manga.consejo: Also used for a hose («manga de riego»). Here it means a shirt sleeve.
p.enviara.consejo: «enviar» becomes «enviara» in the past subjunctive after «que».
p.niego.consejo: From «negar». Its opposite is «afirmar», to say yes.
p.pasen.consejo: In «que me pasen», the subjunctive comes after «que».
p.cinta.consejo: A thin strip, as in «cinta adhesiva», sticky tape.
